label: bm-biopolymer-films
topic: Chitin, silk fibroin, cellulose nanocrystals and other biopolymer actuators: hygromorphic films, measured strain and curvature, and combination with a printed backing
summary: Survey of humidity-driven films from silk, chitosan, cellulose nanocrystals, gelatin and similar. The largest in-plane humidity strain in a cast, stiff, bulk-scale biopolymer film is regenerated silk fibroin at 5.0 to 7.3 percent (10 to 90 percent RH), against roughly 0.2 to 1 percent for stock Formlabs resins (about 1.0 percent linear for Flexible 80A V2 by my conversion of its data-sheet 3 percent volume gain). An 8 um silk layer on 25 um polyimide changes curvature by 13 to 21 cm^-1 and bends in 13 to 44 s, but silk has only been bonded to polyimide, not to printed resin or nylon. Bacterial peptidoglycan swells 27 to 50 percent in thickness with GPa modulus and a glue composite survived 180,000 cycles in about 3 s, but those strains are through-thickness AFM values on nanometre films. Cellulose films swell little (NFC 0.06 to 0.09 percent; CNC 0.04 percent per percent moisture, 0.30 across aligned CNC) and bend only when very thin; chitosan composites bend (3.91 cm^-1; more than 140 degrees in 3 s for a carboxymethyl chitosan/MXene film) without a published strain; for gelatin I could not read any numbers. Two earlier claims: I confirm the Formlabs cube table (Rigid 10K under 0.1 percent water and IPA, Elastic 50A V2 39.2 percent IPA) and I confirm, by reading the data-sheet table by coordinates, that Flexible 80A Resin V2 gains 8 percent mass and 3 percent volume in 1 day in water, which contradicts a blanket reading of 'every SLA resin under 1 percent'. A consistency check against the project's 3/2 curvature ceiling: no measured silk curvature exceeds it, and the sulfonated-silk value would be 92 percent of it if its free strain were about 5 percent.
lay_summary: Some natural materials swell when the air gets humid, and a thin strip with a swelling layer glued to a non-swelling layer curls like a drying leaf. The plastics Formlabs sells swell by only about a fifth of a percent to one percent, so they curl very little. Silk protein cast as a thin film swells by 5 to 7 percent while staying a hard solid, and an 8-micrometre silk coat on a plastic strip (thinner than a hair) curled to a radius under a millimetre in under a minute. Cellulose and chitosan films swell less or have been measured less well, and for gelatin I could not read the numbers. The catch is speed: the thicker the swelling layer, the slower it moves, so silk works as a thin coating on a printed backing and nobody has yet tested that backing with a Formlabs part. The first step would be a cheap bench test, a silk coating on a printed strip, before anything is shown to an architect.

findings.claim: Cast regenerated Bombyx mori silk fibroin films (methanol-treated, freestanding, RH swung 10% to 90%) shrink and swell in length by 5.0 to 7.3 percent. This is the largest in-plane humidity strain I found in a stiff, cast, bulk-scale biopolymer film, and it is 5 to 36 times the 0.2 to 1 percent estimated for stock Formlabs resins.
findings.value: WR strain 5.02 +/-1.05 % (0% PEO), 5.02 +/-0.51 (10%), 5.74 +/-1.01 (20%), 5.93 +/-0.93 (40%), 7.29 +/-0.83 % (60% PEO porogen), 10-90 %RH, linear, n=5; Æ in the quote is the PDF-text-extraction form of +/-

findings.claim: How silk strain was defined: change in film length between 10 percent and 90 percent RH divided by original length, from image analysis over three RH cycles, on 3 mm x 10 mm freestanding films.
findings.evidence_quote: The WR strain is defined as a ratio of deformation (the change in length in response to 10% and 90% RH) to the film’s original length, determined by ImageJ software

findings.claim: Silk/polyimide bilayers (silk cast on a 25 um polyimide film) bend in 13 to 44 s and straighten in 22 to 40 s when RH is alternated between 10 and 90 percent. This is the response time for an 8 um silk layer.
findings.evidence_quote: all silk/polyimide bilayer films took similar time to bend within 13–44 seconds and straighten within 22–40 seconds in response to rapid RH changes

findings.claim: Silk-on-polyimide bilayer with 8 um regenerated silk on 25 um polyimide: the change in curvature between dry and hydrated state is 13 cm^-1 for unmodified silk and 21 cm^-1 after sulfonating its tyrosine residues, i.e. radii of curvature of 0.77 mm and 0.48 mm. For comparison, beech/spruce wood bilayers in the project record reach 0.0087 mm^-1 = 0.087 cm^-1, so these silk bilayers curve 150 to 240 times more tightly (at 33 um instead of about 5 mm total thickness).
findings.value: delta kappa 13 -> 21 cm^-1; h_silk 8 um; h_PI 25 um; 10-90 %RH in 10 min steps
findings.evidence_quote: This difference increased from 13 cm-1 to 21 cm-1 (Figure 1c,d), and raised WR energy density from 1.6 MJ m-3 to 3.5 MJ m-3

findings.claim: Thickness of the silk bilayer in the tyrosine paper: 8 um silk layer on 25 um polyimide (the text prints 3x4x0.025 mm), humid-chamber dried (>90% RH) overnight.
findings.evidence_quote: depositing an 8 µm thick layer of RSF onto 3x4x0.025 mm polyimide films (CAPLINQ)

findings.claim: Silk water-responsive actuation energy density (work per volume, from bilayer curvature) is 1.6 MJ/m3 for methanol-treated silk, 3.0 to 3.1 MJ/m3 for nanoporous silk and 3.5 MJ/m3 for tyrosine-sulfonated silk; mammalian skeletal muscle is quoted at 8 kJ/m3 in one paper and 0.8 kJ/m3 in the other (the two papers disagree by 10x).
findings.source: https://par.nsf.gov/servlets/purl/10422709 (Soft Matter 2023, doi 10.1039/d2sm01601j) ; https://par.nsf.gov/servlets/purl/10616826 (Soft Matter 2025, doi 10.1039/d5sm00040h; accepted manuscript)
findings.evidence_quote: there is a range of porosities that result in silk’s optimal water-responsive energy density at 3.1 MJ m

findings.claim: Silk processing for a cast hygromorph layer: degum cocoons by boiling in 0.02 M sodium carbonate 30 min, dissolve in 9.3 M lithium bromide at 60 C for 2 h, dialyse, cast, dry overnight in a humid chamber (about 90% RH), then immerse in 99.9% methanol for 10 min to lock in beta-sheets; optional PEO porogen is leached in water for one day. Plasma-treated polyimide was the backing.
findings.value: Na2CO3 0.02 M 30 min; LiBr 9.3 M 60 C 2 h; methanol 99.9% 10 min; PEO leach 1 day; plasma 30 s
findings.evidence_quote: Both freestanding and bilayer films were immersed in a 99.9% methanol solution (Sigma-Aldrich) for 10 min.

findings.claim: Tyrosine paper uses a two-step methanol stabilisation (99.9% then 90%, 10 min each) and a diazonium coupling in aqueous silk solution, then dialysis; this is a wet-chemistry route that needs a lab.
findings.evidence_quote: The dry films were immersed in 99.9% methanol (Sigma-Aldrich) for 10 min, followed by immersion in 90% methanol for 10 min, to stabilize the β-sheet structure

findings.claim: Bacillus subtilis peptidoglycan (PG, a sugar-peptide cell-wall polymer) swells in thickness by 50.1 percent (cortex PG) and 27.2 percent (cell-wall PG) when RH rises from 5 to 90 percent, as measured by environmental AFM on nanometre-thick layers. This is the largest humidity strain I found in a stiff polymer, but it is a through-thickness AFM value on 70 to 150 nm layers, not an in-plane value on a bulk film.
findings.value: cortex PG height +50.1 %, volume +65.2 %; cell wall PG height +27.2 %, volume +45.8 %; 5->90 %RH; layer thickness 70.6 nm and 153 nm at 5 %RH
findings.evidence_quote: cortex PG shows a height change of 50.1% and a volume change of 65.2%

findings.claim: Peptidoglycan is stiff: Young's modulus 4.91 GPa at 5 percent RH falling to 1.77 GPa at 90 percent RH (factor 2.8 softening).
findings.evidence_quote: Young's moduli are 4.91 GPa at 5% RH and 1.77 GPa at 90% RH

findings.claim: Peptidoglycan mixed with a commercial craft glue gives a castable composite (1.33 GPa dry, 0.47 GPa at 90% RH) that bends coated Mylar, silicone and PDMS films within about 3 s and survived 180,000 bend/straighten cycles with a reported degradation of 5.17e-5 percent per cycle.
findings.value: E=1.33->0.47 GPa; relaxation tau 2.34 s bend / 2.12 s straighten on Mylar; 180,000 cycles
findings.evidence_quote: the PG/adhesive‐coated Mylar film can respond to RH changes within ≈3 s (Figure 5f ), and bend and straighten over 180, 000 cycles without significant performance degradation

findings.claim: Peptidoglycan headline performance: 72.6 MJ/m3 energy density, 9.1 MW/m3 power density, up to 27.2 percent deformation within 110 ms, actuation pressure about 354.6 MPa. Inside the paper the cortex PG measurement is 59.9 MJ/m3 and the 27.2 percent belongs to cell-wall PG, so the abstract mixes two samples.
findings.evidence_quote: PG can deform as much as 27.2% within 110 ms, and its actuation pressure reaches ≈354.6 MPa.

findings.claim: Bacillus spore monolayers on microcantilevers and elastomer sheets give hygromorph actuators with energy density above 10 MJ/m3 (two orders above synthetic water-responsive materials); mutants roughly doubled it.
findings.evidence_quote: the mechanical response of Bacillus spores to water gradients exhibits an energy density of more than 10 MJ m(-3), which is two orders of magnitude higher than synthetic water-responsive materials

findings.claim: Spider dragline silk fibres can shrink up to 50 percent in length with about two-fold radial swelling at high RH or when wetted (background statement in a Science Advances paper, not measured in this survey); the same paper measures humidity-driven twist up to 255 deg/mm (N. pilipes) between 40 and 100 percent RH. Fibres, not films, so not directly printable.
findings.value: up to 50 % length; twist 255 deg/mm (N. pilipes), 127 deg/mm (A. versicolor)
findings.evidence_quote: dragline silk can shrink up to 50% in length concomitantly with radial swelling (about twofold increase of the diameter)

findings.claim: Nanofibrillated cellulose (NFC) films 8 um thick bend with a steady-state curvature of 0.3 to 0.75 cm^-1 when a 10 to 40 percent RH difference is imposed across the thickness, reaching steady state in tens of seconds. The paper's own estimate of the swelling that explains this is only 0.06 percent (8 um) and 0.09 percent (48 um): cellulose films bend because they are thin, not because they swell a lot.
findings.evidence_quote: the swelling ratio of the 8-µm NFC film is estimated to be only about 0.06%; whereas for the 48-µm film, the swelling ratio is about 0.09%

findings.claim: NFC curvature falls steeply with thickness: about 0.2 cm^-1 at 38 um, minimal at 48 um, and paper of 60 um bends little. This is a gradient-driven (RH differs on the two faces) bend, not a bonded bilayer.
findings.evidence_quote: a thickness of ≈38 µm showed only moderately small bending of about 0.2 cm−1, and the one with thickness of ≈48 µm exhibited only a minimal curvature

findings.claim: Cellulose nanocrystal (CNC) film hygroscopic swelling coefficient: 0.040 percent strain per percent moisture content for self-organised (isotropic) films, and for shear-oriented films 0.02 (parallel) and 0.30 (perpendicular to alignment). Measured by digital image correlation from 0 to 97 percent RH. The wood bilayer coefficient in the project record (beech 3.2e-3 per percent moisture content = 0.32 percent per percent) is about equal to the perpendicular CNC value.
findings.evidence_quote: Self-organized CNC films showed isotropic swelling, CHS ∼0.040 %strain/%C. By contrast, shear-oriented CNC films exhibited an anisotropic swelling, resulting in CHS ∼0.02 and ∼0.30 %strain/%C, parallel and perpendicular to CNC alignment, respectively.

findings.claim: Converting CNC film coefficients to a strain needs the moisture-content change, which I did not retrieve. Illustration only, with an ASSUMED 10 wt percent change: isotropic CNC 0.4 percent, shear-oriented perpendicular 3 percent. The assumed value is unverified background, not a finding.

CNC on polyurethane bilayer (70 um CNC layer with glucose additive on 70 um polyurethane/silver nanoparticle elastomer): horizontal bending angle rises from 0 to 70.5 deg in 60 s of moisture absorption, and in the vertical orientation 0 to 144.2 deg in 14 s; recovery 71 to 80 s; 5000 bend cycles without loss.
findings.value: 70.5 deg / 60 s (horizontal); 144.2 deg / 14 s (vertical); revert 80 s / 71 s; 5000 cycles; layers 0.07 +/-0.01 mm each
findings.evidence_quote: the horizontal bending angle of the actuator increases from 0° to 70.5° as the moisture absorption time increases from 0 to 60 s, and then it takes 80 s to revert to its original position

findings.claim: The CNC/PU film has a coffee-ring cracking problem: pristine CNC layers crack within hundreds of bend cycles; adding glucose gives crack-free films after 5000 cycles. Humidity step magnitude (RH values) is not stated in the main text I read; actuation force 299.4 Pa at a bending angle of 76.5 deg.
findings.evidence_quote: after subjected to 5000 bending cycles, the actuator still exhibited stable actuating performance, revealing excellent structural stability

findings.claim: Chitosan (82.7 percent deacetylated, from crab-shell chitin) / 50 wt percent multiwalled carbon nanotube cast films, 20 to 40 um thick, bend away from a moist source and back towards a dry one; 100 cycles with no obvious fatigue; 25 x 4 x 0.04 mm strips. No curvature or strain value is given in the main text I read.
findings.evidence_quote: (film length = 25 mm, width = 4 mm, and thickness = 40 μm) in response to moist and dry stimuli by adsorption and desorption of water molecules

findings.claim: Chitosan films on a carbon nanotube/PDMS layer give a humidity-driven curvature of 3.91 cm^-1 (3.84 cm^-1 with near-infrared light); the PDMS supplies the mechanical support. Thickness, RH step and cycle count are not in the abstract and I could not read the full text.
findings.evidence_quote: for an ultra-large actuation curvature (3.91 cm-1 in humidity actuation, 3.84 cm-1 in light actuation)

findings.claim: Carboxymethyl chitosan (a chitosan derivative) / MXene composite film with a thickness gradient bends beyond 140 degrees within 3 s under a 40 percent RH difference across the film, with over 1000 self-oscillation cycles; tensile strength 39.9 MPa. The MXene is an inorganic conductive filler, so this is not a pure biopolymer film.
findings.value: >140 deg in 3 s; dRH 40 %; >1000 cycles; tensile 39.9 +/-0.9 MPa
findings.evidence_quote: with a bending angle exceeding 140° within 3 s

findings.claim: Gelatin: the only gelatin-specific hygromorph paper located is Kumar, Siraj and Satapathy, Materials Advances 2024, 'Vapor selective and controlled actuation of gelatin-based soft actuators'. The publisher blocked every automated fetch, so I could read only the title and a one-line abstract and obtained no curvature, strain, thickness, response time or cycle numbers. A search-engine summary mentioned about 7 mN lifting force under water vapour and 25x own weight under ethanol vapour; I could not verify that from the page.
findings.evidence_quote: Soft actuators with multi-vapour responsiveness demonstrating distinct movement.

findings.claim: Chitin: no humidity-actuated film made directly from chitin or chitin nanofibres was found (Europe PMC title search for chitin AND actuator/humidity/moisture returned 3 unrelated records). Chitosan, its deacetylated form, is the only chitin-derived polymer with humidity actuators located.

Formlabs cube test (1 cm cube, 24 h) confirms the earlier agents: water uptake of Rigid 10K is under 0.1 percent, Flexible 80A Resin 0.7, Elastic 50A V2 0.7, Clear Resin V5 0.9, and isopropyl alcohol uptake of Elastic 50A V2 is 39.2 percent versus under 0.1 for Rigid 10K. Acetic acid 5 percent (chitosan's solvent is 1 percent acetic acid): Rigid 10K under 0.1, Elastic 50A V2 1.5, Flexible 80A 0.9. Methanol is not in the Formlabs table.
findings.value: IPA: Rigid 10K <0.1, Elastic 50A V2 39.2, Flexible 80A 11.7; acetone: Rigid 10K <0.1, Elastic 50A V2 43.4; water 0.7 / <0.1
findings.evidence_quote: Rigid 10K Resin :: Acetic Acid 5% <0.1; Acetone <0.1;

findings.claim: CONTRADICTION with a blanket reading of the earlier resin-chemistry file ('every current SLA resin gains under 1 percent mass in water at 24 h'): that holds for the 1 cm cube table (which has a row for Flexible 80A Resin, not V2), but Formlabs' own Flexible 80A Resin V2 data sheet (ASTM D471 slabs) gives +8 percent mass and +3 percent volume after 1 day in deionised water and +9 percent mass, +7 percent volume after 1 week, with 26 Shore A points softening. I confirm this figure of the spec-formlabs-materials file by reading the table cells by coordinates. The two Formlabs tests use different specimens, so 0.7 and 8 are not the same quantity.
findings.value: Flexible 80A V2, DI water: 1 day +8 % mass +3 % volume -26 Shore A; 1 week +9 % mass +7 % volume -27 Shore A
findings.evidence_quote: Flexible 80A Resin V2 TDS ASTM D471, label Deionized Water spans these two rows (y=396 and y=405): 1 day -26 +8% +3% 94% 89% ; 1 week -27 +9% +7% 101% 88%

findings.claim: Own calculation: the best stock soft resin (Flexible 80A V2, 3 percent volume gain in 1 day) corresponds to about 1.0 percent linear swelling if isotropic ((1.03)^(1/3)-1), 2.3 percent after 1 week. Silk's 5.0 to 7.3 percent in-plane strain is 5 to 7 times that, and 25 to 36 times the 0.2 percent estimated for the Clear/Rigid pair.

Own calculation with the project-record Timoshenko ceiling kappa_max = 1.5 d_eps / h: for a 1 mm bilayer, 1 percent differential strain gives at best 15 m^-1 (radius 67 mm), silk's 5.02 percent gives 75 m^-1 (radius 13 mm), 7.29 percent gives 109 m^-1 (radius 9 mm). For 0.3 mm total thickness: 50, 251 and 365 m^-1.

Own check of the 3/2 ceiling against measured silk curvature: for the 33 um silk/polyimide bilayer, 13 cm^-1 requires a differential strain of at least 13e2 x 33e-6 / 1.5 = 2.9 percent and 21 cm^-1 requires at least 4.6 percent. Using the free-film strain of unmodified silk (5.02 percent, different films and batch) the ceiling is 22.8 cm^-1, so the unmodified bilayer reaches 57 percent of it. The 21 cm^-1 sulfonated-silk value would be 92 percent of the ceiling if that silk strained about 5 percent; its free-film strain was not reported, so this is a consistency check, not a test. No measured curvature exceeds the ceiling.

Own scaling estimate (diffusion-limited, tau proportional to h^a with a = 1.3 to 2): the 13 to 44 s bend time of an 8 um silk layer becomes 6 to 114 min for a 100 um silk layer and 2 to 190 h for a 1 mm layer. Silk is therefore a thin-coating technology; a thick silk layer would be as slow as the printed resins.

key_claims.claim: Cast silk fibroin films strain 5.0 to 7.3 percent in length between 10 and 90 percent RH, far above the 0.2 to 1 percent of stock resins (and above the roughly 1 percent linear equivalent of the best soft resin, Flexible 80A V2).

A silk-on-backing bilayer works with a thin silk layer: 8 um silk on 25 um polyimide gives a 13 to 21 cm^-1 curvature change and bends in 13 to 44 s. The only backing tested is polyimide; no printed resin or nylon backing has been tested.
key_claims.evidence_quote: This difference increased from 13 cm-1 to 21 cm-1 (Figure 1c,d), and raised WR energy density from 1.6 MJ m-3 to 3.5 MJ m-3

key_claims.claim: Cellulose by itself is not a large-strain material: nanofibril film swelling is about 0.06 to 0.09 percent and the CNC isotropic coefficient 0.040 percent per percent moisture; only shear-aligned CNC across the alignment (0.30) approaches wood-like values.
key_claims.evidence_quote: the swelling ratio of the 8-µm NFC film is estimated to be only about 0.06%; whereas for the 48-µm film, the swelling ratio is about 0.09%

key_claims.claim: The statement that stock Formlabs resins gain under 1 percent in water holds for the 1 cm cube table but not for Flexible 80A Resin V2 on its own data sheet (ASTM D471: +8 percent mass, +3 percent volume in 1 day).
key_claims.evidence_quote: Flexible 80A Resin V2 TDS ASTM D471, label Deionized Water spans these two rows (y=396 and y=405): 1 day -26 +8% +3% 94% 89% ; 1 week -27 +9% +7% 101% 88%

recommendations: Run one bench coupon before any design work: cast regenerated silk fibroin (target 10 to 50 um) on a post-cured Rigid 10K strip 0.2 to 0.4 mm thick (IPA-wipe, optionally plasma), methanol-stabilise, and measure curvature at 30, 60, 90 percent RH. Compare with the 3/2 ceiling: for a 0.3 mm total thickness and 5 percent strain it is about 250 m^-1 (radius 4 mm).

Keep the active layer thin. Time grows roughly as thickness to the power 1.3 to 2, so 8 um bends in under a minute but a 1 mm silk layer would take hours to days (own scaling estimate). Design the printed part as the stiff, thin backing, not as the swelling layer.

Do not put Elastic 50A or Silicone 40A through the methanol step: Elastic 50A takes up 39 percent IPA and Silicone 40A 5.9 percent, against under 0.1 percent for Rigid 10K (Formlabs table), and methanol is untested. Rigid 10K is the safest backing; chitosan (cast from 1 percent acetic acid) is gentler, since 5 percent acetic acid costs Rigid 10K under 0.1 percent.

Measure, do not borrow, the silk modulus and free strain on your own films, and check whether the 21 cm^-1 sulfonated silk is near the 1.5 d_eps / h ceiling; this gives a second, independent test of the Lean-checked bound on a real biopolymer.

Treat cellulose as a stiffening or anisotropy tool, not as the motor: NFC and isotropic CNC swell 0.04 to 0.09 percent; only aligned CNC across the alignment (0.30 percent per percent moisture) approaches wood.
Obtain the gelatin paper (Kumar 2024) through a library or by contacting the authors before claiming anything about gelatin.

glossary.plain: A material or shape that changes shape when the air gets more or less humid.
Two layers stuck together, one that swells and one that does not, so the pair bends.
The structural protein of silkworm silk, which can be dissolved and cast into films.
A plastic-like sugar polymer made from the shells of crabs and shrimp (from chitin).
Tiny rod-shaped crystals of plant cellulose that can be dried into a film.
The sugar-and-protein mesh that forms the wall of bacteria.
How tightly something bends: one divided by its radius of bend.
How full of water vapour the air is, from 0 to 100 percent.
How much a length grows, as a percentage of the original length.
How much work a material can do per cubic metre when it swells.
A liquid plastic that a laser or light hardens layer by layer.
Plastic powder melted into shape by a laser, such as nylon.
A proven upper limit: a two-layer strip cannot curve more than 1.5 times the strain difference divided by its thickness.
A short alcohol bath that makes silk film stop dissolving in water.
Cleaning a solution by letting small salts pass out through a membrane.

could_not_find: Gelatin: no curvature, strain, thickness, response time or cycle numbers. The only gelatin hygromorph paper found (Kumar 2024, doi 10.1039/D4MA00015C) is on rsc.org, which returned HTTP 403 to every automated fetch, and Europe PMC does not hold it.

Chitin: no humidity-actuated film from chitin or chitin nanofibres turned up; chitosan is the only chitin-derived polymer with actuators found, and the chitosan papers fetched give no hygroscopic strain or curvature at a stated RH step (except 3.91 cm^-1 for chitosan on CNT/PDMS, abstract only).

Humidity strain in percent for CNC films: Shrestha 2017 gives a coefficient per percent moisture content, and I did not retrieve the moisture-content change, so CNC strain at a stated RH step is not known (the 0.4 and 3 percent figures use an assumed 10 wt percent and are labelled as such).

Young's modulus of cast silk film at dry and humid conditions. A search-engine summary quoted 7.2 GPa (methanol-treated silk) and 2.5 GPa for polyimide from Jung 2021 (doi 10.1039/D1SM00794G); rsc.org blocked the fetch, so those numbers are unverified and only used to bracket the modulus ratio n in a sensitivity table.

Any silk, chitosan, CNC or gelatin layer cast on a cured Formlabs resin or a sintered nylon surface. All silk bilayers found use plasma-treated polyimide. Adhesion, wetting of printed resin by aqueous silk, and survival of the printed part in the methanol or acetic acid step are untested in the literature I found; my statements on Rigid 10K vs Elastic 50A in these solvents are inferences from the Formlabs IPA, acetone and acetic-acid columns, since methanol is not tested by Formlabs.

Cycle life above 100 cycles for chitosan, above 5000 for CNC, and any cycle count for silk bilayers (neither silk paper states one). Peptidoglycan/glue composite is the only system with a six-figure count (180,000 cycles).
Humidity step magnitude in the CNC/polyurethane paper (main text does not give the RH values; supplementary data not read) and in the chitosan/CNT paper (nitrogen at nominal 100 and 0 percent RH).

Peptidoglycan strains are through-thickness AFM values on 70 to 150 nm layers; an in-plane strain of a printed or cast PG-glue layer was not given, and PG cannot presently be sourced in bulk for a building.

Paywalled or blocked, not read in full: Kumar 2024 (RSC), Jung 2021 (RSC), Chen 2014 Nat Nanotechnol full text, Xu 2019 J Mater Chem B full text. The Nat Nanotechnol and J Mater Chem B entries rest on their abstracts.

Headroom: free C: was 514 MB (below the 1 GB limit), so I ran no heavy local command; all downloads were under 3.5 MB and went to D:. One request to the Unpaywall service used that service's own public example address in its URL (not a personal address) and returned nothing useful.

Disagreement kept, not smoothed: muscle energy density is 8 kJ/m3 in Jung 2023 but 0.8 kJ/m3 in Khan 2025; peptidoglycan headline 72.6 MJ/m3 vs 59.9 MJ/m3 cortex measurement inside the same paper; Flexible 80A uptake 0.7 percent (cube table, older Flexible 80A Resin row) vs 8 percent (V2 data sheet, D471).
